assumptions.title: Assumptions & Notes
assumptions.body:
• This calculator is for Assessment Year 2025-26 (Financial Year 2024-25).
  • It assumes you are a salaried individual.
  • The New Tax Regime is the default regime. You must explicitly opt for the Old Regime if it is more beneficial.
  • Standard Deduction of ₹50,000 is applied to salary income under both regimes as per latest rules.

comparison_table.title: Old vs New Regime: Key Differences
comparison_table.description: Here’s a quick look at what’s allowed under each regime.

checklist.title: Which Regime Should You Choose?
checklist.body:
• Choose the Old Regime if: You have significant deductions like HRA, home loan interest, and utilize the full 80C limit. Typically, if your total deductions are above ₹2.5 - ₹3.75 lakh, the old regime is often better.
  • Choose the New Regime if: You have few or no deductions, prefer simplicity, and want lower tax rates at most income levels without the hassle of tracking investments for tax purposes.

how_we_calculate.title: How We Calculate Your Tax
how_we_calculate.body:
Old Regime: We first calculate your total deductions, including HRA exemption and all sections (80C, 80D, etc.). This is subtracted from your gross income to get your 'Taxable Income'. Tax is then calculated based on the old tax slabs, which vary for different age groups.

New Regime: The calculation is simpler. We only apply the standard deduction of ₹50,000 to your salary. No other deductions are allowed. Tax is then calculated based on the new, lower tax slabs. For a detailed breakdown of slabs, you can refer to the official Income Tax Department website.

scenario1.title: Young Professional Renting in a Metro (Salary: ₹12 Lakh)
scenario1.body: With full 80C (₹1.5L) and 80D (₹25k) deductions, plus HRA exemption, the Old Regime is likely better, saving significant tax.

scenario2.title: Homeowner with a Home Loan (Salary: ₹20 Lakh)
scenario2.body: With ₹2L home loan interest deduction, 80C, 80D, and NPS, the Old Regime is almost certainly more beneficial due to the large volume of deductions.

scenario3.title: Investor with Low Deductions (Salary: ₹15 Lakh)
scenario3.body: If you don't have HRA or a home loan and only make minimal 80C investments, the New Regime's lower slab rates will likely result in lower tax payable.

faqs.question: Which tax regime is the default for FY 2024-25?
faqs.answer: The New Tax Regime is the default option for all taxpayers. If you want to opt for the Old Regime, you must do so specifically when filing your Income Tax Return (ITR).

faqs.question: Can I switch between the old and new regimes every year?
faqs.answer: Salaried individuals can choose between the old and new regimes every financial year. However, individuals with business income can only switch once in their lifetime.

faqs.question: Is the standard deduction of ₹50,000 available in the new tax regime?
faqs.answer: Yes, from FY 2023-24 onwards, the standard deduction of ₹50,000 is available for salaried individuals and pensioners under the New Tax Regime as well.

faqs.question: How does choosing the old regime affect my investment planning?
faqs.answer: The old regime allows deductions under Section 80C, making investments in PPF, NPS, and ELSS more tax-efficient. Use our mutual fund screener to find ELSS funds that qualify for 80C deductions.

faqs.question: What if I have a home loan? Which regime should I choose?
faqs.answer: If you have a home loan, the old regime is typically better due to home loan interest deductions. Use our loan optimizer to compare loan options and maximize your tax benefits under the old regime.

faqs.question: How does the tax regime choice impact my retirement planning?
faqs.answer: Your tax regime choice affects long-term savings. The old regime favors tax-saving investments, while the new regime offers simplicity. Use our retirement corpus calculator to plan your retirement corpus considering your tax regime choice.

faqs.question: Can I compare my tax savings with different investment options?
faqs.answer: Yes, use our FD vs PPF calculator to compare fixed deposits with PPF, and our mutual fund overlap calculator to optimize your investment portfolio for maximum tax efficiency.
